Definition: from G746 and G2409; the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest:--chief (high) priest, chief of the priests.
BiblicalUsage: The high priest is the chief priest, and the word carries both the office and its failure. Caiaphas, high priest that year, says it is expedient that one man die for the people, and Jesus is led to Caiaphas the high priest; but Hebrews says we have a great high priest passed into the heavens, holy, harmless, undefiled, and separate from sinners.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the contrast is the whole point. Caiaphas used the office to kill, and Christ fills the office to save, and the better high priest is the one who lives forever to intercede for us.
